c01.display: Welcome back to NLP, Simply Explained. This is unit 3, lesson 3: transition-based parsing.
c01.spoken: Welcome back to N L P, Simply Explained. This is unit 3, lesson 3: transition-based parsing.

c02.display: Last time we learned what a dependency tree looks like. Today we see how a fast parser builds one, a single move at a time.
c02.spoken: Last time we learned what a dependency tree looks like. Today we see how a fast parser builds one, a single move at a time.

c03.display: Here's the idea. Read the sentence from left to right, and build the tree using just a few simple moves.
c03.spoken: Here's the idea. Read the sentence from left to right, and build the tree using just a few simple moves.

c04.display: A transition parser reads words from a queue called the buffer, keeps words it's still working on in a pile called the stack, and picks one move at each step.
c04.spoken: A transition parser reads words from a queue called the buffer, keeps words it's still working on in a pile called the stack, and picks one move at each step.

c05.display: At any moment, you can describe where it is by what's on the stack and what's left in the buffer.
c05.spoken: At any moment, you can describe where it is by what's on the stack and what's left in the buffer.

c06.display: Think of sorting post. New letters wait in your in-tray, that's the buffer, and letters you're still dealing with sit in a pile on your desk. That's the stack.
c06.spoken: Think of sorting post. New letters wait in your in-tray, that's the buffer, and letters you're still dealing with sit in a pile on your desk. That's the stack.

c07.display: The version in your syllabus is called arc-eager. It has four moves.
c07.spoken: The version in your syllabus is called arc-eager. It has four moves.

c08.display: SHIFT pushes the next word from the buffer onto the stack.
c08.spoken: shift pushes the next word from the buffer onto the stack.

c09.display: LEFT-ARC makes the next word the head of the word on top of the stack, then pops that top word off. Its job is done.
c09.spoken: left arc makes the next word the head of the word on top of the stack, then pops that top word off. Its job is done.

c10.display: RIGHT-ARC makes the top word the head of the next word, then pushes the next word onto the stack.
c10.spoken: right arc makes the top word the head of the next word, then pushes the next word onto the stack.

c11.display: And REDUCE pops the top word, once it has its head and all its dependents.
c11.spoken: And reduce pops the top word, once it has its head and all its dependents.

c12.display: Let's parse "Priya ate pizza". We start with ROOT on the stack, and all three words in the buffer.
c12.spoken: Let's parse "Priya ate pizza". We start with root on the stack, and all three words in the buffer.

c13.display: Step one, SHIFT: Priya moves onto the stack.
c13.spoken: Step one, shift: Priya moves onto the stack.

c14.display: Step two, LEFT-ARC: the next word, ate, becomes the head of Priya. Priya is the subject, so she's popped off.
c14.spoken: Step two, left arc: the next word, ate, becomes the head of Priya. Priya is the subject, so she's popped off.

c15.display: Step three, RIGHT-ARC: ROOT becomes the head of ate, and ate goes onto the stack.
c15.spoken: Step three, right arc: root becomes the head of ate, and ate goes onto the stack.

c16.display: Step four, RIGHT-ARC: ate becomes the head of pizza, the object. The buffer is empty, and the tree is complete.
c16.spoken: Step four, right arc: ate becomes the head of pizza, the object. The buffer is empty, and the tree is complete.

c17.display: But how does the parser know which move to make? Here's the loop.
c17.spoken: But how does the parser know which move to make? Here's the loop.

c18.display: Look: check the word on top of the stack, the next words in the buffer, and the links made so far.
c18.spoken: Look: check the word on top of the stack, the next words in the buffer, and the links made so far.

c19.display: Score: a trained classifier gives a score to each possible move.
c19.spoken: Score: a trained classifier gives a score to each possible move.

c20.display: Act: make the move with the best score.
c20.spoken: Act: make the move with the best score.

c21.display: Repeat: keep going until the buffer is empty.
c21.spoken: Repeat: keep going until the buffer is empty.

c22.display: And how is that classifier trained?
c22.spoken: And how is that classifier trained?

c23.display: Start with a treebank: sentences whose correct trees are already known.
c23.spoken: Start with a treebank: sentences whose correct trees are already known.

c24.display: For each one, work out the sequence of moves that would build that exact tree. The rule that does this is called the oracle.
c24.spoken: For each one, work out the sequence of moves that would build that exact tree. The rule that does this is called the oracle.

c25.display: Then train a classifier to predict the oracle's move from what it sees at each step.
c25.spoken: Then train a classifier to predict the oracle's move from what it sees at each step.

c26.display: So what's good about it, and what isn't?
c26.spoken: So what's good about it, and what isn't?

c27.display: Strengths: it makes one pass from left to right, using about two moves per word, so it's very fast. And it's easy to give the classifier new clues.
c27.spoken: Strengths: it makes one pass from left to right, using about two moves per word, so it's very fast. And it's easy to give the classifier new clues.

c28.display: Limits: it never goes back, so an early mistake can't be undone. And the basic version can only build projective trees, the ones without crossing links.
c28.spoken: Limits: it never goes back, so an early mistake can't be undone. And the basic version can only build projective trees, the ones without crossing links.

c29.display: Quick quiz. In arc-eager parsing, which move puts the next word onto the stack without adding any link?
c29.spoken: Quick quiz. In arc-eager parsing, which move puts the next word onto the stack without adding any link?

c31.display: It's SHIFT. It simply moves the next word from the buffer onto the stack.
c31.spoken: It's shift. It simply moves the next word from the buffer onto the stack.

c32.display: Let's recap. A transition parser keeps a stack and a buffer, and makes one move at a time.
c32.spoken: Let's recap. A transition parser keeps a stack and a buffer, and makes one move at a time.

c33.display: Arc-eager has four moves: SHIFT, LEFT-ARC, RIGHT-ARC and REDUCE.
c33.spoken: Arc-eager has four moves: shift, left arc, right arc and reduce.

c34.display: A classifier chooses each move, trained by copying an oracle.
c34.spoken: A classifier chooses each move, trained by copying an oracle.

c35.display: It's very fast, but it never goes back to fix a mistake.
c35.spoken: It's very fast, but it never goes back to fix a mistake.

c36.spoken: Next lesson: Word Vectors. How can a computer know that 'rain' is close to 'storm'?
